# Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1

## Overview
Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 is a well-studied strain of the opportunistic pathogen P. aeruginosa. It serves as a reference strain for understanding bacterial pathogenesis and antibiotic resistance.

## Key Features
- **Genome Size**: ~6.3 Mb
- **Genes**: ~5,500 protein-coding genes
- **Strain Type**: Clinical isolate, reference strain
- **Pathogenicity**: Opportunistic pathogen

## Research Significance
This strain is crucial for:

- **Antibiotic Resistance**: Understanding mechanisms of drug resistance
- **Biofilm Formation**: Model for studying bacterial biofilms
- **Virulence Factors**: Research on pathogenicity mechanisms
- **Quorum Sensing**: Cell-to-cell communication studies

## Clinical Importance
- Common cause of hospital-acquired infections
- Major pathogen in cystic fibrosis patients
- Known for multi-drug resistance
- Important target for new antimicrobial development
